_doc: Red Reaches field NPCs (consumed by game/world/common/npc_life.gd). Roles come from game/canon/regions/red_reaches.json (ambient.npcs, side_quests, descent_events); names marked 'new' are invented bit-parts that fill canon roles (drover, Free Scale contact, Dominion clerk, stranded hauler). Schema: stations[{p:[x,z],act,face:[dx,dz]}], schedule{dawn|day|dusk: station index}, hotspot{label,r,y_off}, quest (region side quest id handed to RegionRunner), events (region descent events this NPC owns - their stand-alone sites are hidden), talk[] first matching entry wins ({first, state: open|locked|done, if, if_not, lines[], quest, play_event, choices[{text, actions[], reply[], reply_fail[]}]}), barks[] ({text, if, if_not, phase}). Visual: game/art/models/npcs/npc_registry.json (real model scene) else a baked FallbackVisual silhouette from shape/h/r/body/acc/head.

lines.text: You are standing in my light. Move left. Left. Good.
Sixteen generations of Keths have cranked this line. I am the sixteenth. I am not tired. I am annoyed. It is different.
Handlers. Good. Someone who can carry a stone.
The contractor left a brochure. Do you know what a brochure is? It is a promise printed on something that will not hold water.
Wells stay when people do. Mind the third crank, it bites.
Three apprentices. Crooked, crooked, fine. That is how a line is taught.
Water by evening. A seal on every cistern. I drink it. I do not thank it.
The rig is quiet. The wells hum a little under my feet. Water remembers things the rest of us forget.
The Line does not need you to like it. It needs you to leave the stones where they are.

barks.text: Water is not a thing you own. It is a thing you owe.
Wells stay when people do.
Noon. Shade. Nobody speak to me for an hour.
Crooked. Re-lay it. Again.

lines.text: Easy. Hands low. The sentinel is watching you, and she decides for the herd.
A road collapse cut my grazers off from the lichen terraces. A week, maybe, before they start to fail.
They are still out there. The sentinel keeps her head up. That is how I know it is bad.
We took the long way, on foot. Slow. Nobody lost. That is the whole trick of herding.
The road holds. First trip over it, the sentinel dropped her head. I nearly wept. Do not tell her.
I do not talk about the gap. Graze on, friends. Graze on.
The sentinel stopped watching the horizon yesterday. First time all season. I sat down and did nothing for an hour.
Dust grazers keep the Waystation basin open. Without them it would be scrub by spring.

barks.text: One sentinel, always. She drops her head when the herd is safe.
Watch the wedge. They move as one animal.
The herd is whole.

hotspot.label: Talk to the Free Scale scout

lines.text: Do not look at the scarf. Look at the road. Free Scale does not own this road. Nobody does. That is the point.
I count Dominion carts and I note which stones they take. No politics. Just arithmetic.
The Thoughtstone is open. Past it there is a Spanwright vault. Closed is still working, they say. Let it work.
The pylons are quiet. My tally says the Dominion lost a week. I will take a week.
Free tip. Stand in the old ruin's shadow and push at the capstone, the loose one. People stopped looking there a century ago.
The big rig is down. Nobody on my side did that. Note it. Note who did.
Native pathways, native hands. Walk softly and take only what the road offers.

barks.text: Four carts east, empty. Eight west, loaded. Note it.
No institution should own a pathway.
Dominion survey flags, ninety-one this week.

lines.text: My plate is whole again. The valley is long. Walk it with something to carry.
Cart axle went at the narrows. I can drag it. I cannot drag it and eat at the same time.
A scrap of lichen culture would do. I shed plates every season. I will pay in plate.

reply.text: Good. Slate plate, fresh shed. Do not tell the others I gave you the nice one.

reply_fail.text: Nothing in the satchel? Then take the thought. Mites ticked by the cracks east of here, that is where lichen grows.

reply.text: A hand on the rope is worth a month of advice. Take this soil, off the grazer trail.
Road is long. I will manage. I always manage.

barks.text: Axle. Of all the things, an axle.
Slow is a speed.

lines.text: Do not just stand there admiring my flour. Unless you are going to lift.
Axle-deep and one pair of hands. A day's flour sacks, tied on top, and the road wants it back.
Cart rolls. Flour goes north. Dust goes everywhere else. You are all right, Handler.
Flour goes north again, and the Span held. I would like to buy whoever held it a bowl of stew.
The road keeps what it is given. I intend to give it one cart at a time.

barks.text: Brace. Lift. Brace. Lift.
A cart road is a promise with ruts in it.
Who tied this knot? Me. Of course me.

lines.text: A claim on the Red Span wreck. Staked, filed, legal in three jurisdictions and one I invented. Handler, you look like you read the fine print.
Under the stumps: a cache of cut Thoughtstone. The yard calls the place a grave. I call it inventory.
Still thinking? The stone is not going anywhere. Neither, sadly, is the yard.
Claim struck. I lost a week of margin and gained a lecture. Net: even.
Half to the families. I do not enjoy it. I do sleep better. Do not tell the Undermarket.
Pleasure doing business. The yard will not speak to either of us. I have grown fond of the quiet.
The Span is still standing. Bad for the salvage trade. Good for everything else. Do not quote me.
I have a permit for everything. Ask me about the permit for permits.

barks.text: Everything is for sale. Not everything should be.
A grave is only a claim nobody has filed yet.
Fair price. Never a fair share. Different words.

lines.text: Do not pull the permit. I know it is a bad permit. I did not write it.
The plate beetles keep throwing themselves at the survey pylons. I was told to keep them out of the dig. I do not know how.
You are back. The beetles are back too. They never left.
Below their hearing. Quiet as a bad rumor. I filed it as a calibration. Nobody asked what for.
The dig continues. I do not recommend looking at the pit floor.
Power cell gone, nobody saw. Funny. I have not slept this well in a year.
AUGUR-7 is down. My permit is void and my contract is a rumor. I have not felt this light since training.
Survey is not a crime. It is only a way of saying: this is mine, in numbers.

barks.text: Four more pylons to calibrate. Forty minutes of sleep to ration.
The beetles lean on the slate at dusk. I used to find that funny.
I am only the instrument.

lines.text: Permit seven-one-four covers every rock in this basin. If you are carrying a rock, I need the form.
I am not a villain. I am a stamp. The stamp does not get to choose, but it does get to be accurate.
Your pump contract is filed. Dominion seal on every cistern. The aquifer schedule is quarterly. Please do not read the appendix.
A power cell is missing. I am required to ask. I am also required to record that nobody answered.
The pylons are down. Form nine, loss of equipment. Someone will sign. It will not be me.
Form nine-A, catastrophic equipment loss. Seventeen signatures required. Nobody wants to be the sixteenth.
Stand behind the yellow line. If you cannot find the yellow line, stand behind me.

barks.text: Stamp. Stamp. File.
Form nine-C. Where did I put form nine-C?
It is not corruption if it is on letterhead.

lines.text: Do not look at the sketch! ...Fine. Look. It is an arch. For the yard's gate. I want it to be remembered.
The yard's pylons are rotting under the gate. Everyone says so. Nobody says it to the arch.
Still deciding about the arch? I am. For the record, I have been deciding for a month.
I sketch arches in the dust and rub them out when someone looks. It is a ritual. It is not a good one.
I still think it looks incredible. I also know what is inside it. Both are true.
It looks incredible. Nobody has mentioned the pylons. I mention them every night to the wall.
Pylons first. Arch later. My teacher said that is the whole job. I said that is half. She said: which half.
The Span sang apart and then it did not. I am still thinking about the load path. I am always thinking about the load path.
The Span from here looks like a held breath. I am learning not to hold mine.

barks.text: Wider at the base. Always wider at the base.
I still think it looks incredible.
Do not look at the sketch.

lines.text: Hum. B-flat, a little sharp. The cable is fine. The foundation is the one humming wrong.
Market day crossings draw thousands. I want an evacuation drill. The guild says it will cost a day's trade.
Hum. Still B-flat. Still sharp. Still waiting on your answer.
I check the cable by plucking it. If it hums wrong, I hum back. Quietly. So the Span does not take offence.
Practice makes boring. Boring is a gift.
The guild is pleased. The cable is not. I will be here, plucking, in case it has an opinion.
You stood on the weakest span and promised. I wrote it in the log. In ink.
Hum. B-flat. Flat. Truly flat, for the first time in a month. I could weep. I will not. I am on duty.
Mind the third pier. It rings a little when it is thinking.

barks.text: Hum. B-flat.
Practice makes boring. Boring is a gift.
Tension is a kind of listening.

lines: Vesk. The axle is mine. The flour is mine.
I only want to know how much the sack weighs, for the record.
It weighs what it weighs. Go record somewhere else.
Dahl, form nine-C. Beetle incident. Sign here.
There is no box for 'they are not wrong'.
Then it goes in comments. Nobody reads comments.
Count of carts, east: four. Herd count?
Free Scale thanks you. Free Scale also lacks a budget.
